notes.text: 2025 yield 22.50 t/ha (+11.9%), best block; Jan–Mar 2026 5.09 vs 5.50 t/ha (-7.5%).
Most harvesting rounds in 2025 (20.5, 85% of target); mild Mg and K deficiency.

summary: Jan–Mar 2026 FFB 2,106.76 t, 4.54 t/ha vs 4.60 t/ha Jan–Mar 2025 (-1.3%); P98 and P13A fell, P11 rose (Agro).
2025: 8,845.68 t FFB, 19.06 t/ha per Agro (PA prints 18.80) vs 20.01 in 2024 (-4.7%); 15.5% below the 10,463 t budget.
2025 cost RM261.78/t FFB vs RM201.00/t budget; general charges RM1,560.52/ha vs RM911.49/ha budget (Pinfosys under-budgeting, PA).
Harvesting is the weak point: 15.0 rounds (Agro) or 18.5 (PA) vs 24 budgeted, intervals up to 28 days in P98/P02 in Jan–Mar 2026, though harvesters are 23 of 23.
Fields upkeep generally acceptable; bagworm low, cattle intrusion unresolved; P98 replant 2028, P02 2029 (Agro).

issues.title: PA yield 18.80 t/ha is wrong; 2025 was 19.06
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 section 8 prints 18.80 t/ha and says 6% below 2024's 20.01. FFB 8,845.68 t over 464 ha is 19.06 t/ha (Agro Table 13: 19.06, -4.7%); the PA's own CPO yield 3.62 t/ha at 19% OER also gives 19.06.

issues.title: PA budget yield 20.41 t/ha does not match budget tonnes
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 gives budget FFB 10,463 t on 464 ha, which is 22.55 t/ha, not 20.41. On tonnes, 8,845.68 t is 15.5% below budget, not the 8% the PA states (8.1).

issues.title: Replanting: none planned (PA) vs P98 2028, P02 2029 (Agro)
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 para 2.2 says there are no replanting plans. Agro 1/2026 para 2.4 and Table 2 schedule P98 (74 ha) for 2028 and P02 (74 ha) for 2029, with P98 fertiliser to stop in 2027.

issues.title: Harvesting rounds and interval differ
issues.detail: PA 7.2: 18.5 rounds in 2025 vs 24 budget. Agro Table 14: average 15.0 rounds (62% of target). PA 7.3 says interval averaged 13 days (May 2026) while Agro Tables 6 and 10 show 6-31 days in Jan–Mar 2026 and over 20 days in P98/P02.

issues.title: P02 inter-rows: unsatisfactory (PA) vs acceptable (Agro)
issues.detail: PA 6.3.2 (13 May 2026) calls P02 inter-rows unsatisfactory and wants urgent spraying and VOP eradication; Agro 5.5 (13 Apr 2026) says weeding quality acceptable in P98 and P02.

issues.title: Bagworm blocks and control differ
issues.detail: PA 6.5.2: two cypermethrin rounds at P11A, P11B, P13A, P13B, no fresh infestation. Agro 4.12: defoliation signs in P12 and P13, and estate records show no control done in 2026 so far.

issues.title: Agro Table 8 rat percentages do not match counts
issues.detail: Of 200 palms: P11A 14 = 7.0% (printed 7.5%); P12B 12 = 6.0% (6.5%); P13A 11 = 5.5% (6.5%); P13B 13 = 6.5% (6.6%). PA 6.5.1 says no rat damage seen, whereas the census shows 5.0-9.0% new damage, all below the 10% threshold.

issues.title: Agro says other months under 1.5 t/ha, January was 1.69
issues.detail: Agro 4.3 says only March exceeded 1.5 t/ha (1.74), but Appendix 2(b) January 2026 is 784.64 t, about 1.69 t/ha on 464 ha.

issues.title: P98 share of estate: 1% (text) vs 15.95% (table)
issues.detail: Agro 2.4 says P98 (74 ha) is about 1% of the estate; Table 2 shows 15.95% for P98 and for P02 (74 of 464 ha).

issues.title: P13A 2024 yield 19.67 vs 19.62
issues.detail: Agro Table 13 shows 19.67 t/ha; Appendix 2(a) 1,000.78 t over 51 ha is 19.62, which also matches the +8.2% change printed.

issues.title: Production cost table budget figures differ by RM30
issues.detail: PA section 9 shows budget upkeep RM960,301 and harvesting RM719,857; sections 6 and 7 show RM960,331 and RM719,887.

issues.title: 2026 manuring percentages may use pre-revision programme
issues.detail: Agro Table 5 requires 375.00 t Mix B, about 9.0 kg/palm over 41,685 palms in P11-P13, but Appendix 1 (revised) shows 6.75 kg/palm (three rounds of 2.25 kg). The 25% applied may not reflect the revised programme.

actions.item: Cut harvesting interval to 15 days or less; raise rounds toward 24 a year
Improve harvester productivity and work hours (5-6.5 h vs 9 h); keep harvesters
Raise sprayer productivity (circle 3.8 ha/man-day vs 4.5-5.0 target; 8 vs 12 pumps)
Urgent selective spraying and VOP eradication in P02 (and P98)
Bagworm census and control; resolve cattle intrusion
Finish 2026 manuring (RP not yet received; Mix B 25% applied to Mar); follow revised programme strictly
Apply spare urea at 1 kg/palm in P12A, P12B or P13A
Road grading with compaction when company approves (RM17/chain, 2026/27)
Investigate the 2013 planting bunch weight change (12.9 to 16.0 kg)
Report leaf analysis for 2026 in next Agronomy report
Replant P98 in 2028 and P02 in 2029; stop P98 fertiliser in 2027
Monitor and explain general charges overspend in 2026
Draw up 2027 fertiliser programme after field inspection in second half of 2026

kb:
LADANG BATU SABLAS, Ria Gemilang Sdn Bhd (Prosper group). Fact pack drawn from two reports. (1) PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisory Report, Planting Advisor Mr. Boey Chee Weng, visit 13 May 2026, reviewing January to December 2025). (2) Agronomy Report 1/2026 (Agronomist En. Muhammad Ghazali Abdul Ghani, Junior Agronomist, signed with Mr. Chong Kuan Ming, Senior Agronomist; visit 13 April 2026; follow-up to the 23 October 2025 visit; Manuring Programme 2026). Plantation Controller Dr. Chua Chin Kok (Agro). Senior Manager En. Zulkarnain Bin Barik. Estate Manager Mr. Robin A/L Sinnappanah. Period note: PA financial and crop figures cover Jan-Dec 2025; Agro yield figures cover full year 2025 and Jan-Mar 2026. Money in RM.

AREA (PA 1/2026 section 2, no change in the area statement). Mature 464.0 ha (95.67%), total planted 464.0 ha, no immature. Unplanted (jungle) 8.00 ha (1.65%), labour quarters 13.0 ha (2.68%), total 484.99 ha. All planting material Yangambi DXP. Fields (ha): P98 1998 74; P02 2002 74; P11A 2011 47; P11B 2011 64; P12A 2012 44; P12B 2012 64; P13A 2013 51; P13B 2013 46. PA 2.2: no replanting plans for this estate. Agro (section 2, Tables 1-3): block system unchanged and suitable for leaf sampling. About 68% of area is prime-age palms; 16% aged 20-25 years and 16% over 26 years. Tentative replanting: P98 (74 ha) in 2028, P02 (74 ha) in 2029; fertiliser programme for P98 to cease in 2027. Agro text says P98 is about 1% of estate area, but its Table 2 shows 15.95% for each of P98 and P02 (74 of 464 ha). No recent palm census (Agro 2.5); density 136-140 palms/ha in P98, P02, P11, P12 and 119-121 palms/ha in P13 sub-blocks. Palms per field (Agro Table 3): P98K 10,064 (136/ha); P02L 10,064 (136); P11A 6,392 (136); P11B 8,960 (140); P12A 5,984 (136); P12B 8,704 (136); P13A 6,171 (121); P13B 5,474 (119).

LABOUR (PA 1/2026 section 3, as of Dec 2025). Total workers 38 against 41 required (-3). Harvesters 23 against 23 required (ratio 1:20 ha, adequate). Manuring workers 3 of 3. Spraying workers 4 of 4. Spraying mandore 3 of 3. Manuring mandore 1 of 1. Drivers 2 of 2. Loaders 0 of 2 (short 2). Security guards 2 of 3 (short 1). Worker to planted ha ratio 1:12 ha, adequate. PA comment on labour in 2025 cycle: harvesters and field workers adequate. The Group MD asked that the contractor be guided on work arrangements, worker welfare and salary payment, and that estate management reduce harvester turnover. PA 12.1: harvesters should earn high wages through high productivity and work 9 hours a day; PA 7.7 says harvesters work only 5 to 6.5 hours. Agro 5.2: first-quarter 2026 intervals in old plantings were hurt by weather and lower harvester output during public holidays; Agro 6.4 mentions harvester absenteeism and weather disruptions.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA section 5, Jan-Dec 2025). Actual RM724,081.03 against budget RM422,931.00, i.e. RM1,560.52/ha against RM911.49/ha. Management and supervision RM269,092.31 (budget RM187,660; RM579.94/ha vs RM404.44). Labour and amenities RM168,285.73 (budget RM160,895; RM362.68/ha vs RM346.76). Other expenditures RM261,124.01 (budget RM66,940; RM562.77/ha vs RM144.27). MSPO RM25,578.98 (budget RM7,436; RM55.13/ha vs RM16.03). PA 5.2: overspend caused by under-budgeting of certain account codes in Pinfosys against the old-system budget. PA 5.3: Estate Manager advised to monitor over-expenditure in 2026 and give reasons.

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA section 6, Jan-Dec 2025). Total RM930,510 against RM960,331 budget (underspent 3%), RM2,005.41/ha vs RM2,069.68/ha. Per ha actual vs budget: weeding 203.29 vs 201.14; manuring 1,561.48 vs 1,491.59 (RM724,525 vs RM692,097); pest and disease 9.70 vs 69.85 (RM4,500 vs RM32,412); census and thinning 4.09 vs 11.94; drains 7.70 vs no budget (RM3,575); roads and bridges 94.50 vs 140.54; boundary, survey, fences 0.44 vs 30.71; pruning 124.22 vs 123.91. PA 6.4.1: fertiliser cost overspent because urea was bought on the Chairman's instruction to be applied in the field to deter cattle intrusion.

WEEDING (PA, 2025). Circle spraying 1,244 ha (2.7 rounds, 100% of budget; 2 rounds for old plantings, 3 for younger mature). Circles generally clean except P02 (partly clean, some due for spraying). Method Inter pump; output 3.8 ha/man-day (normal at least 4.5; Group MD asked above 5.0); piece rate RM20/ha; earnings RM76/man-day; glyphosate 0.38 l/ha (2.3 pumps/ha); 8 pumps per man-day (could be 12). Selective spraying 1,244 ha (2.7 rounds, 100%). Inter-rows generally clean with some soft woodies and VOPs, but P02 not satisfactory (urgent selective spraying and VOP eradication required) and P98 had overgrown VOPs in a photo. Mist blower output 4 ha/man-day; RM20/ha; earnings RM80/man-day; Garlon 0.29 l/ha (2.3 pumps/ha); 10 pumps per man-day acceptable. Agro (Mar 2026, Tables 7 and 11): first round of inter-row spraying 100% complete in all fields; first circle round complete in P13 and in progress in P11, P12 and old plantings; quality acceptable, minimal broadleaf weeds, soft grasses predominant in P98 and P02; field maintenance satisfactory.

MANURING 2025 (PA section 6.4 and Agro Table 4). PA: 2,414 ha or 100% of the 2,414 ha budget applied; fertiliser programme completed. Manuring by wheelbarrow, 30 bags/man-day, RM2.50/bag, earnings RM75/man-day (satisfactory). Agro Table 4 (2025): Mixture A required 130.70 t, 100%; Mixture B 301.85 t plus 66.90 t carried forward, 100%; kieserite 38.75 t, 100%; rock phosphate 62.10 t, 100%; total 533.40 t, 100%. Agro 3.1: manuring completed fully in 2025, but the second round of Mixture B for P12B was 3 months behind schedule.

MANURING 2026 (Agro section 3, as of March 2026, Table 5). Required 579.45 t: NK1 110.60 t (45.25 t received and applied, 41%), Mixture B 375.00 t (99.45 t received, 93.80 t applied, 25%), kieserite 31.30 t (all received, 13.55 t applied, 43%), rock phosphate 62.55 t (none received or applied, 0%). Total received 176.00 t, balance to receive 403.45 t, applied 152.60 t (26%). Agro 3.3: first Mix B round done in P12A and P12B though 2 months behind schedule; kieserite completed for P13 by March; first NK1 application completed for P98 and P02. Agro: 2026 programme revised because of substantial fertiliser price rises and limited stock; 2027 programme to be drawn up after the field inspection in the second half of 2026.

REVISED 2026 FERTILISER PROGRAMME (Agro Appendix 1, grams per palm; months read from the table layout). P98: NK1 2500 g. P02: NK1 2000 g (two 2000 g entries appear; months not legible). P11 and P12: Mix B 2250 g Jan, kieserite 750 g Mar, Mix B 2250 g Apr, rock phosphate 1500 g Jun, Mix B 2250 g Aug. P13: Mix B 2250 g Feb, kieserite 750 g Mar, Mix B 2250 g May, rock phosphate 1500 g Jun, Mix B 2250 g Sep. Mix B is 45% SOA, 40% MOP, 14% kieserite, 1% borate; RP 28-30% P2O5; kieserite 27% MgO. Note: the Table 5 Mix B requirement of 375 t equals about 9.0 kg/palm over P11 to P13 (41,685 palms), while Appendix 1 shows 6.75 kg/palm, so the percentages in Table 5 may be measured against the pre-revision programme.

PEST AND DISEASE. PA 6.5 (visit 13 May 2026): no rat damage seen; two rounds of cypermethrin sprayed at P11A, P11B, P13A and P13B for bagworm and no fresh infestations seen; Ganoderma minimal and sporadic (photos of upper stem rot and fruiting bodies in P02); cattle intrusion still unresolved, cattle suspected of carrying bagworm into the estate; PA group MD comment: stay vigilant and run bagworm census to find instar stage. Agro (13 April 2026): rat census (Table 8, 200 palms per block) new damage P11A 14 palms (printed 7.5%), P11B 18 (9.0%), P12A 12 (6.0%), P12B 12 (printed 6.5%), P13A 11 (printed 6.5%), P13B 13 (printed 6.6%); P98 11 (5.5%), P02 10 (5.0%). All below the 10% threshold; baiting not required; quarterly monitoring advised. Bagworm defoliation signs in P12 and P13, severity much reduced, empty pupal casings and inactive larvae; no pest control carried out in 2026 so far per estate records. Ganoderma negligible in old plantings. Mild Mg and K deficiency symptoms in P12B, P13A, P13B, with sporadic orange fronds in terrace and hilly areas (low cation exchange capacity); leaf analysis for 2026 to be reported next time.

ROADS (PA): 2,000 chains grading budgeted at RM10/chain, none done (not effective without compaction; on hold due to diesel price; RM17/chain with compaction in 2026/27); roads acceptable (Agro: 2026 maintenance delayed by rain). No drain budget.

PRUNING (PA section 6.8; Agro 4.6, 5.4). Progressive pruning 5,568 ha of 5,568 ha budgeted (100%), appearance satisfactory. Rates per palm per year: RM1.20 for 1998 and 2002, RM0.80 for 2011-2013. Agro: canopy standards acceptable, no over- or under-pruning; old plantings pruning improved significantly in Q1 2026.

HARVESTING AND COLLECTION (PA section 7, Jan-Dec 2025). Cost RM660,986 against RM719,887 budget: RM74.72/t FFB against RM68.80/t. Harvesting labour RM377,266 (RM42.65/t vs 41.56); internal transport RM181,393 (RM20.51/t vs 19.24); incentive RM67,753 (RM7.66/t vs 8.00); top-up wages RM34,574 (RM3.91/t, no budget) for new harvesters. PA 7.2: 18.5 rounds achieved against 24 budgeted, extending intervals and causing crop loss. PA 7.3: interval averaged 13 days at the May 2026 visit, some blocks 17 days due to rain. Outturn 96%. Two mini dumpers (2 cutters and 1 collector) in use; the others broken and too costly to repair, so wheelbarrows used. Output per harvester 1.43-2.07 t/man-day by block (PA 7.6), earnings RM48.62-71.34/day vs basic wage RM65.39; rates RM34/t (2011-2013), RM41-42/t (1998, 2002). Agro 2025 rounds (Table 14, target 24): P98 13.0; P02 14.0; P11A 13.0; P11B 14.0; P12A 13.5; P12B 16.5; P13A 14.0; P13B 20.5; average 15.0 (62%). Rounds to March 2026 (Table 16): P98 4.5; P02 3.5; P11A 3.0; P11B 3.0; P12A 3.5; P12B 5.0; P13A 2.5; P13B 3.0; average 3.5 (58% of target). Harvest intervals in days, Jan / Feb / Mar 2026 (Tables 6 and 10): P11A 11-20, 17-20, 9-21; P11B 6-17, 10-22, 8-18; P12A 18-26, 14-23, 9-19; P12B 17-31, 10-24, 9-19; P13A 6-18, 8-25, 7-21; P13B 7-23, 10-18, 9-21; P98 13-28, 13-25, 21-28; P02 16-24, 16-28, 23-27. Agro asks for intervals of 15 days or less. No crop backlog seen in old plantings (no harvesting observed). Over-ripe bunches in P11B.

CROP PRODUCTION (PA section 8, Jan-Dec 2025, 464 ha). FFB 8,845.68 t against annual budget 10,463 t; same period 2024 was 9,285.52 t. CPO 1,680.68 t (budget 1,987.97 t; 2024 1,764.25 t), OER 19.00%. Kernel 353.83 t, 4.00%. PA prints FFB yield 18.80 t/ha against budget 20.41 and 20.01 for 2024; CPO yield 3.62 t/ha. However FFB 8,845.68 t divided by 464 ha is 19.06 t/ha, which is the figure in Agro Table 13, and 10,463 t over 464 ha is 22.55 t/ha, not 20.41 (see data caveats). PA 8.3: shortfall mainly due to shortage of harvesters early in the year. PA 8.4: low cropping season, mostly male flowers. Bunch weights Dec 2024 to Dec 2025 (PA): 1998 23.4 to 20.2 kg; 2002 22.7 to 22.1; 2011 16.8 to 16.8; 2012 15.9 to 16.6; 2013 12.9 to 16.0. Weight loss attributed to over-ripe bunches from extended intervals; the 2013 jump needs investigation.

YIELD PERFORMANCE (Agro section 6). Table 13, full-year yield t/ha 2024 to 2025 (change): P98 17.98 to 16.60 (-7.7%); P02 18.33 to 18.13 (-1.1%); P11A 21.36 to 18.58 (-13.0%); P11B 22.41 to 18.83 (-16.0%); P12A 22.62 to 20.97 (-7.3%); P12B 19.37 to 18.08 (-6.7%); P13A 19.67 (Appendix 19.62) to 21.23 (+8.2%); P13B 20.10 to 22.50 (+11.9%); estate 20.01 to 19.06 (-4.7%). Estate yield history t/ha (Appendix 2a): 2021 16.99; 2022 14.98; 2023 15.55; 2024 20.01; 2025 19.06. Estate FFB: 2021 7,882.98 t; 2022 6,949.55; 2023 7,213.05; 2024 9,285.52; 2025 8,845.66. Table 15, Jan-Mar 2026 vs Jan-Mar 2025 t/ha: P98 3.17 vs 5.02 (-36.9%); P02 3.74 vs 3.86 (-3.1%); P11A 5.95 vs 4.31 (+38.1%); P11B 5.32 vs 4.11 (+29.4%); P12A 6.07 vs 5.60 (+8.4%); P12B 4.14 vs 3.99 (+3.8%); P13A 4.10 vs 5.02 (-18.3%); P13B 5.09 vs 5.50 (-7.5%); estate 4.54 vs 4.60 (-1.3%), 2,106.76 t. Monthly FFB 2026: Jan 784.64 t, Feb 513.29 t, Mar 808.83 t. Agro 4.3: first three months of 2026 were 4.54 t/ha, March the highest at 1.74 t/ha, other months said to be under 1.5 t/ha (but January is 784.64 t, about 1.69 t/ha). Agro 6.1: yield fell 4.7% in 2025 with most sub-blocks lower except P13A and P13B. Agro 6.3: Q1 2026 1.3% lower than Q1 2025 due to a drastic fall in P98 and P13A. Agro 6.2 and 6.5: crop recovery suboptimal due to harvesting frequency; agronomic condition of old and prime palms acceptable; bagworm to be watched.

PRODUCTION COST (PA section 9, Jan-Dec 2025). Total RM2,315,577 = RM261.78/t FFB against RM201.00/t budget (budget total RM2,103,089). General charges RM81.86/t vs RM40.42; upkeep and cultivation RM105.19/t vs RM91.78; harvesting and collection RM74.72/t vs RM68.80. PA 9.1: cost high because the crop budget was not achieved (and general charges overspent). Production cost table prints budget upkeep RM960,301 and harvesting RM719,857, while sections 6 and 7 show RM960,331 and RM719,887.

RAINFALL (PA Appendix 1 and Agro Appendix 3). Total mm and rain days: 2021 1,871.00 mm, 128 days; 2022 2,369.00, 116; 2023 2,335.00, 145; 2024 2,256.10, 165; 2025 2,313.00, 130. 2026 to March: Jan 32.00 mm (2 days), Feb 219.00 (8), Mar 133.00 (7), total 384.00 mm in 17 days.

DATA CAVEATS. (1) PA prints 18.80 t/ha for 2025; arithmetic and Agro give 19.06 t/ha. (2) PA budget yield 20.41 t/ha does not match 10,463 t over 464 ha (22.55 t/ha); on tonnes FFB was 15.5% below budget, not 8%. (3) PA says no replanting plans; Agro schedules P98 in 2028 and P02 in 2029. (4) Rounds in 2025: 18.5 (PA) vs 15.0 (Agro). (5) P02 inter-rows unsatisfactory in PA (May) but acceptable in Agro (April). (6) Rat census percentages in Agro Table 8 do not match counts for P11A, P12B, P13A, P13B. (7) Agro Table 13 shows P13A 2024 yield 19.67, Appendix 2a gives 19.62.
